headline: OpenVLHarness reports broad gains from visual evidence tools and persistent multimodal memory
summary: An Oct 19 arXiv preprint introduces OpenVLHarness, a training-free multimodal agent stack with nine task-level capabilities, outputs rendered as inspectable evidence, and per-query memory that keeps images, structured results and web references reusable across turns. Across 22 benchmarks and eight open/proprietary backbones, the authors report 9.7-12.6 point average gains over matched no-tool baselines. In their GPT-6 Luna comparison, medium-effort OpenVLHarness averages 56.5 versus 48.0 for the base model at maximum effort, 48.6 for Codex at maximum and 48.8 for Visual Sketchpad at maximum. These are author-reported benchmark results: Qwen3-VL results average three runs, while proprietary-model results are single runs; no independent reproduction was conducted. Model-token accounting excludes tool execution and judging, and the paper's abstract/prose cost summary conflicts with Table 2 for Codex.
